findings.description: The database password is embedded in EC2 user data and written into a PHP configuration file. User data is retrievable by principals with instance describe access and may be exposed through the instance or Terraform state, broadening access to the database credential.
No metadata_options block requires IMDSv2, so the instance can use IMDSv1. An SSRF flaw on the web server could retrieve the attached instance-role credentials without IMDSv2 token protection.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network address. Although the shown security group limits MySQL ingress to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-facing routing and can become externally reachable if security-group controls change.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage, backups, and snapshots unencrypted at rest.

This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to 0.0.0.0/0. It allows unrestricted outbound communication, creating data-exfiltration and command-and-control paths from the database.

The application instance role grants every S3, EC2, and RDS action against every resource. Compromise of the web server or its role credentials would enable broad account-level data access and infrastructure modification.
